title: Adaptive Windows, Foldables, ChromeOS, and Input Check

questions.prompt: Which approach best applies adaptive windows, foldables, chromeos, and input?
options: Respond to live window and capability state, preserve the task, and support touch plus non-touch input without device-name assumptions.
questions.answer: Respond to live window and capability state, preserve the task, and support touch plus non-touch input without device-name assumptions.
questions.explanation: The correct response preserves authority, compatibility, exact artifact evidence, adverse-path behavior, and operational ownership.

questions.prompt: A foldable device always requires placing content in two panes separated by its hinge.
questions.explanation: Checking smallestScreenWidth once at startup misses live window resizing, multi-window, fold posture, and external-display changes.

questions.prompt: Why is window size more useful than device category?
questions.answer: The app renders into a changeable window whose size and features may not match a fixed phone, tablet, or foldable label.
questions.explanation: The answer identifies the contract or mechanism that remains valid beyond one implementation demonstration.
